hints.title: Offline Query Processing
hints.text: Queries can be answered in increasing order of their threshold values.

hints.title: Priority Traversal from Top-Left
hints.text: Always expand the reachable cell with the smallest grid value first.

hints.title: Incremental Reachability Count
hints.text: For each sorted query, pop all reachable boundary cells with value less than the query value, expand unvisited neighbors, and accumulate points.

hints.title: Sorted Offline Heap Expansion Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def maxPoints(self, grid: list[list[int]], queries: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        sorted_q = sorted((q, idx) for idx, q in enumerate(queries))
        ans = [0] * len(queries)
        pq = [(grid[0][0], 0, 0)]
        visited = [[False] * n for _ in range(m)]
        visited[0][0] = True
        count = 0
        for q_val, q_idx in sorted_q:
            while pq and pq[0][0] < q_val:
                val, r, c = heapq.heappop(pq)
                count += 1
                for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
                    nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                    if 0 <= nr < m and 0 <= nc < n and not visited[nr][nc]:
                        visited[nr][nc] = True
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (grid[nr][nc], nr, nc))
            ans[q_idx] = count
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(m * n log(m * n) + k log k)
complexity.notes: Each grid cell is pushed and popped from heap at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running a full graph traversal for every query takes O(k * m * n).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(m * n) space stores visited states and boundary priority queue.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorts queries offline and uses Dijkstra-like min-heap to expand reachability monotonically.
